new_candidates.body:
Problem overview

Bullet's default allocators can pass a null pointer to memset after an
allocation failure. For a nonzero allocation size, these unchecked memory
initialization calls cause undefined behavior and can crash the host process.

Affected version

Confirmed by source inspection in Bullet 3.2.5 and master at commit
d3afe76132fc76b0f9b2359cbaef47a3766e7fbb. No runtime crash reproduction was
executed for this report. The affected memset path is the generic allocator
implementation; the platform-specific aligned allocator branches differ.

Native API and failure-path evidence

In src/LinearMath/btAlignedAllocator.cpp:

1. btAllocDefault calls malloc(size), then immediately calls memset(data, 0,
   size), without checking the allocation result.
2. The generic btAlignedAllocDefault calls sAllocFunc. If it returns null,
   the else branch assigns null to ret, but execution still reaches
   memset((char*)ret, 0, size). For a nonzero size, this is an invalid memory
   access and can crash the process.

Source:
https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/d3afe76132fc76b0f9b2359cbaef47a3766e7fbb/src/LinearMath/btAlignedAllocator.cpp#L22-L75

Minimal reproduction

The following source-based probe injects a failing allocation without requiring
memory exhaustion or robot assets. It has not been executed for this report.
Use the generic allocator path with BT_HAS_ALIGNED_ALLOCATOR,
__CELLOS_LV2__, and BT_DEBUG_MEMORY_ALLOCATIONS undefined.

```cpp
#include <cstddef>
#include <LinearMath/btAlignedAllocator.h>

static void* failAllocation(std::size_t) { return nullptr; }
static void freeNothing(void*) {}

int main()
{
    btAlignedAllocSetCustom(failAllocation, freeNothing);
    (void)btAlignedAlloc(16, 16);
}
```

The inspected implementation routes this call through btAlignedAllocDefault
and reaches memset(nullptr, 0, 16).

Actual impact

A failed native allocation can cause undefined behavior and terminate the host
process inside memset during native object construction.

Downstream context

A downstream entry point is Tesseract 0.35.0 makeCastCollisionObject. Its
compound-shape branch constructs btCompoundShape with the dynamic AABB tree
enabled. The Bullet constructor calls btAlignedAlloc(sizeof(btDbvt), 16),
which reaches the allocator above. This allocation happens inside the
constructor, after the outer std::make_shared allocation.

Sources:
https://github.com/tesseract-robotics/tesseract/blob/0.35.0/collision/bullet/src/bullet_utils.cpp#L1277-L1282
https://github.com/tesseract-robotics/tesseract/blob/0.35.0/collision/bullet/include/tesseract/collision/bullet/bullet_utils.h#L65
https://github.com/bulletphysics/bullet3/blob/3.25/src/BulletCollision/CollisionShapes/btCompoundShape.cpp#L18-L34
new_candidates.title: Null pointer passed to memset after allocation failure in Bullet default allocators
